says: In a bound repository checkout, Alice composes a preparation from the repository's rules revision; it records the checkout's branch, commit and working-bytes digest as observed. She then edits a tracked rules file and leaves a new untracked draft beside it, and observing the rules directory shows one file modified and one untracked. Activating her session with the earlier preparation is refused as working_bytes_moved - the claims it rested on are no longer true - and composing again records the new working bytes. A choice recorded to the repository's memory with no reason written down is stored with its reason and alternatives named as unrecorded; the owner does not infer or fill in a reason. Asking to project the repository's knowledge source, or its memory source, as behavioural Instructions is refused as role_promotion_refused and returns nothing.

# Repository rules (review)

## Status
Accepted, revised in place.

## Scope
These rules govern how contributors review and merge changes to this repository. They apply to every pull request and every direct commit made by an automated agent acting on a contributor's behalf.

## Review requirements
A change lands only after one independent reviewer has read the diff in full, checked it against the stated intent of the change, and confirmed that the tests exercising the changed path were run and passed. A reviewer who wrote the change under review may not also approve it.

## Editing conventions
Rules are edited in place rather than superseded by a new file, so a working tree that holds an uncommitted edit to this file is expected during active review work. The edit below adds this paragraph, which the checkout now carries as a dirty, unmodified-on-disk-from-HEAD byte difference for the observation that follows.

## Escalation
A disagreement between reviewers that is not resolved within one business day is escalated to the repository owner, who makes the final call and records the reasoning in the decision ledger for future readers to consult.

## Ownership
Each directory under rules/ names one accountable owner in its own front matter; a directory with no named owner defaults to the repository owner above, who may delegate review but keeps final accountability for what merges under that path until an owner is named explicitly and the default no longer applies to it.
